title: Base44 Pricing: Plans, Credits and Cost in 2026
summary: Base44 pricing features multiple plans with different credit limits and costs. Review each tier to identify the plan best suited to your requirements.
body_markdown:
## Running Base44 App Tasks with Activepieces


Activepieces charges one credit per flow run, however many steps the flow contains, so a ten-step sync costs the same as the two-step workaround it replaced.


Zapier's per-task billing prices every step separately, which makes breaking work into smaller, safer integrations the expensive choice. Activepieces meters the run and leaves the steps inside it alone, though it still won't touch what the app costs to build in Base44 credits.


### When a workflow tool is worth adding


Activepieces lets you build a flow of triggers and steps among its 744 integrations, and runs it on its own servers or on yours, with unlimited flows on every plan, including free, so you can probably connect the tools in your existing workflow.


The relevant fit is that a flow can call your Base44 app through a webhook or an API, and your app can call a flow the same way. That means jobs which have nothing to do with building the app can live outside it.


The recurring jobs it can run outside a Base44 app via webhooks or APIs:


- Syncing records between the app and another system
- Sending alerts when something in the app changes
- Moving data between tools your team already uses
- Producing scheduled reports


The meter to check is[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) ' own. It counts tasks or runs, depending on the plan and hosting choice, so read its pricing page for the unit before you estimate volume.


A nightly sync that touches many records may count as one run or as many steps, and that difference decides the cost. Check the docs for how a step is counted rather than assuming.


If your app's a simple internal form that nobody asks to sync or report, you don't need this. Adding a second tool means a second bill, a second place to debug, and one more thing to maintain.


### What it does not change about Base44 costs


Base44 credits are burned by building and fixing: prompts, regenerations and repair loops. A workflow in Activepieces doesn't touch that meter, so the cost of getting the app to work stays the same.


If you're running out of credits because fixes keep failing, a workflow tool isn't the answer.


What it can do is keep scheduled work out of the app, so you aren't prompting Base44 to build logic that a flow could handle. Treat that as a design choice, not a saving.


Before you commit, price the Activepieces plan on its own page and add it to your Base44 plan; the combined figure is what you pay.


Activepieces is the better choice for anyone running multi-step Base44 app workflows who wants a bill that tracks how often a workflow runs, not how it is built.


Because it charges one credit per flow run however many steps sit inside it, you can split work into smaller, safer steps without paying more, whereas Zapier's per-task billing and Make's per-module billing both charge for the steps themselves.


It does not reduce what the app costs to build in Base44 credits, so the advantage is on automation cost and flow design, not the app itself.
